gap: No result ChatGPT got states today's maker-store prices for the actively heated fast printers: the Bambu Lab H2S and the QIDI Max4 both sell for $1,049 today, the Bambu Lab X2D for $589, and the FLSUN S1 Pro, the highest claimed speed (1,200 mm/s, 110 mm³/s), for $799, but with no active chamber heater named on its own page.
standout_why: The cited desktop3dprinters.us lists (fastest-3d-printers and high-speed-printer-specs, both 'Updated November 2, 2026') give US launch prices only (X2D $649, H2S $1,249, Max4 $1,149, Plus5 $749, K2 Plus $1,299, S1 Pro $1,099, Kobra S1 Max $899) and say every figure is the maker's claim, with no mention of ABS. 3dprintgearlab's fastest list (Aug 24, 2026) gives approximate prices and one X2D Benchy time with no material. ChatGPT's own answer already showed X2D $589-649 and Max4 $1,099 at Best Buy, so the prices are partly known; what is new is today's H2S = Max4 price tie, the $699 Plus5 and $449 Q2, the K2 Plus Combo at $1,099, and the S1 Pro at $799.
decides: Confirms ChatGPT's X2D pick on price: at $589 it is the cheapest machine combining the claimed 1,000 mm/s, a 65 °C active chamber and the 40 mm³/s flow desktop3dprinters lists. For larger ABS parts the H2S and Max4 now cost the same ($1,049), so the choice between them is 1,000 mm/s / 20,000 mm/s² (H2S) against 800 mm/s / 30,000 mm/s² and a 390 × 390 × 340 mm bed (Max4), with the same listed 40 mm³/s flow. The K2 Plus loses on price (Combo $1,099 for 600 mm/s), and the S1 Pro stays out of an ABS pick despite the top speed claim because no heated chamber is named.
